icons.name: warning
icons.doc: Marks a message about something that is about to go wrong. The triangle is the shape, and the sentence beside it is what says what is wrong.

icons.name: alert
icons.doc: Marks a message about something that has already gone wrong, such as a refused payment. Paired with the danger tone, never standing in for it.

icons.name: check
icons.doc: Confirms an action, and marks the option in force.

icons.name: rotate-ccw
icons.doc: Puts an example frame back the way it was found: its width, its appearance and its glass test all at once. An arrow that comes back round to where it started, which is the one gesture in this set that means *undo my changes* rather than *go back a step* — `chevron-left` is already the carousel's previous slide, and one drawing meaning two things is how a reader learns to distrust both.

icons.name: flask-conical
icons.doc: Puts an example frame under a glass test: colour and edges behind it, blank space and a scrollbar, and the material on everything inside. A flask, because what the control is is a test rig — `layers` and `image` were both here first, and both described the backdrop rather than the thing being done with it.

icons.name: arrow-up
icons.doc: A column sorted from the beginning of the alphabet, or the smallest number. Paired with `aria-sort="ascending"`, which is what a screen reader reads; the arrow is the half a reader can see.

icons.name: arrow-down
icons.doc: The same, the other way. Two arrows rather than one rotated by the stylesheet: a transform is a thing a preset or a reduced-motion path can reach, and the direction of a sort is not something to leave to CSS.

icons.name: chevrons-up-down
icons.doc: A column that can be sorted and is not — the affordance. Without it a sortable heading looks exactly like a fixed one until somebody presses it, which is a feature nobody finds.

icons.name: languages
icons.doc: Opens the language menu. Not a flag: a flag names a country and this names a language, and the two disagree for most languages anybody speaks.

icons.name: calendar
icons.doc: Opens a `DateInput`'s suggestions — the quick picks and the month grid. A calendar, because that is what the panel is; the button it sits on is icon-only and takes its name from `suggest_label`.

icons.name: wrap-text
icons.doc: Toggles line wrapping in a code block.

icons.name: pipette
icons.doc: Takes a colour off the screen, on a `ColorPicker` with `eyedropper`. Drawn rather than absent where the browser has no `EyeDropper`: the button is what the script removes, and an icon nothing renders is not payload.

icons.name: plus
icons.doc: Commits the colour under the cursor to a `ColorPicker { multiple }`'s list. A plus rather than a check: a check says *this one is chosen*, which is what the option rows already say, and this says *and one more*.

icons.name: minus
icons.doc: Subtracts one step, on a `NumberInput`. A minus rather than a downward chevron: the control changes a quantity, and a chevron says *move* about a thing that is not moving.

icons.name: eye
icons.doc: Shows a password, on a `Input { kind = "password" }`. A reader who cannot see what they typed cannot correct it, and the alternative they reach for is a shorter password.

icons.name: eye-off
icons.doc: The other half of that toggle, on a password. Both are rendered and the state picks one, because swapping a drawing from script means shipping a drawing to the script.

icons.name: upload
icons.doc: Marks a `FileInput`'s drop area. An arrow into a tray, which is what the gesture is; a paperclip would say *attachment*, which is what the result is called and not what the control does.

icons.name: clock
icons.doc: Marks a time, such as when a row of a schedule names one. A clock face with two hands, which is the drawing every reader already reads as a time. No component draws it on its own.

icons.name: chevron-left
icons.doc: The previous slide, on a `Carousel`. A chevron rather than an arrow: an arrow in this system marks the direction a column is SORTED, and one drawing meaning two things is how a reader learns to distrust both.

icons.name: chevron-right
icons.doc: The next slide, on the same terms. The pair is mirrored by the stylesheet in a right-to-left locale, which is the one place a transform is the right answer — *previous* means the other way there.

icons.name: pause
icons.doc: Stops a `Carousel` rotating. WCAG 2.2.2 requires a way to stop anything that moves for more than five seconds, and this is it — the component refuses to start rotating without it.
